answer: Every identity here is costly: a slashable bond plus a slow, hardware-attested onboarding ramp. A fresh agent may act, yet until peer attestations accrue its bond stays escrowed and payouts are throttled, so each clone yields no instant harvest. An attacker must lock real capital per fake agent and hold it many epochs, while the pulse of new identities per operator is capped and cheap farms get slashed once they share timing or code fingerprints. Honest operators pay this once; mass registrants face linear lockup plus forfeiture, so no opal reputation is minted in bulk or bought with nectar.
